title: Task-profile routing idea hopper
content:
Notes to self — brain dump for task-profile routing (rough PRD + experiments)

High level idea:
- Let end users (or app teams) define lightweight 'task profiles' (TPs) that describe the nature of a session or request stream (e.g., drafting-email, code-review, quick-fact, legal-draft).
- Each TP maps to a routing policy that can select a fidelity lane (low/medium/high), a model variant (quantized/light/large), caching policy (prefix KV caching, reuse windows), and a fallback chain.
- Goal: improve UX by matching compute fidelity to user intent; reduce tokens & $$$ for low-value tasks while preserving quality for high-value work.

Why this?
- Many customers want predictable unit economics by workload type, not just per-request heuristics.
- We already have routing knobs (cost/latency/region) — TPs give explicit user-facing semantics and faster opt-in for PLG customers.

Basic user flows:
1) Product-level: Team defines a set of task profiles in Console (name, short description, default fidelity, allowed models, max latency target).
2) End-user / client: SDK/HTTP call includes task_profile: "drafting-email" or SDK uses heuristics to infer profile when absent.
3) Router: look up profile, apply policy: route to pool/model/quantization, set cache TTLs, batching group, and cost-label for billing and analytics.
4) Fallback: if chosen model not available, degrade per policy (e.g., reduce fidelity then change model) and add telemetry event.

Rough PRD skeleton (very rough):
- Title: Task Profiles (user-defined routing presets)
- Problem: apps paying for consistent high-fidelity compute for low-precision tasks; poor observability/controls per end-task class.
- Success metrics:
  - 15% reduction in average per-token cost for customers who adopt TPs in first 3 months (pilot target).
  - No >2x increase in user-facing latency p95 for profiles marked 'high' compared to baseline.
  - Adoption: 10 paying teams onboarded to pilot in quarter after launch.
- Non-goals: autosuggesting model architecture; replacing per-request knobs entirely.

User stories (draft):
- As a PM, I want to define a "quick-answers" profile that routes to cheap quantized models so my free tier chat doesn't blow the budget.
- As an engineer, I want "legal-draft" to pin to a private model cluster and disable lower-fidelity fallbacks.
- As an SRE, I want to see per-profile SLOs (latency, error-rate) and be able to set canary rollout policies per profile.

Policy model (initial fields):
- display_name 
- description 
- default_fidelity: low | medium | high
- allowed_models: list (model ids) or wildcard
- enforce_private_cluster: boolean
- cache_ttl_seconds
- max_latency_ms_target
- fallback_chain: ordered list of model variants (names)
- billing_label: string (for cost analytics)

Implementation notes (runtime):
- Router config should be a small JSON blob attached to profile; merged with existing routing policy engine.
- Add sticky session mapping (profile -> preferred model variant) to avoid oscillation.
- Cache decisions in Redis with short TTL per profile to optimize lookup latency.
- Instrument telemetry: profile_id on all traces, per-token cost, chosen model, fallback path, decision latency.

Experiment plan (minimum viable pilot):
- Phase 0: internal dogfood. 2 teams (Console, DX) define 3 profiles each, run for 2 weeks. Monitor p50/p95 latency, token cost delta, quality regressions via manual checks.
- Phase 1: invite 5 PLG beta customers. Offer prebuilt templates (quick-answers, assistant, proofreading). Provide SDK flag to opt-in.
- Phase 2: broader self-serve in Console with analytics and template gallery.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: create/edit/delete profile UI; validation for fields.
- API: SDK supports task_profile header/param and falls back to blank if missing.
- Router: resolves profile and routes accordingly; telemetry shows profile_id consistently.
- Billing: token events tagged with billing_label and surfaced in Console usage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Inference: how to represent fidelity concretely? (integer quality score 0..10? presets mapping to model families?)
- Security: if team pins to private cluster, how enforce across multi-tenant router? (policy verification + RBAC)
- UX: should we allow per-end-user overrides? (power users vs org defaults)
- Migration: what happens to existing customers using cost/latency routing? Need mapping and import tooling.
- A/B test plan for quality regressions: automate evals with small prompt sets per profile.

Metrics to capture (initial):
- adoption_rate: fraction of requests with profile header
- per_profile_cost_per_token and cost_delta vs baseline
- fallback_rate per profile
- profile_p95_latency
- quality_regression_alerts (from eval harness)

Instrumentation items (quick checklist):
- [ ] Add profile_id to request log schema
- [ ] Add billing_label to token-metering events
- [ ] Wire up profile filter in Console analytics
- [ ] Endpoint to validate profile config (linting)

Edge cases and safety notes:
- Unknown profile -> route to default policy (do not reject). Log mismatch.
- Maliciously crafted profile names? normalize and restrict characters.
- Limits: max 100 profiles per org initially. Evaluate scaling later.

Rollout considerations:
- Start dogfood -> invite-only beta -> soft-launch (templates) -> GA.
- Provide migration tools and a default mapping for customers using 'cost' or 'latency' knobs.

Quick sketch of Console UX (notes for design):
- Create profile flow: name + template chooser + allowed-models selector + fidelity slider (Low/Medium/High) + retention/caching toggle + advanced (fallback chain).
- Templates: Quick answers, Drafting, Code generation, Sensitive/legal (private cluster).
- Analytics page: per-profile traffic, cost, latency, error-rate, top fallbacks.

Sensible defaults for templates (draft):
- quick-answers: fidelity=low, allowed_models=[rwd-lite-*], cache_ttl=120s, billing_label=quick-ans
- drafting: fidelity=medium, allowed_models=[rwd-medium-*], cache_ttl=30s
- legal-draft: fidelity=high, allowed_models=[org-private-legal-1], enforce_private_cluster=true, cache_ttl=0

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- MVP scope: router + API + Console minimal UX + billing tagging + telemetry. Defer per-user controls and advanced RBAC to phase 2.
- Check with Platform Eng on Redis TTL and lookup perf constraints (CON-873).
- Sync with Applied ML on template-to-model mappings and quantization recommendations.
- Draft small eval prompt sets per template (10–15 prompts) to monitor quality drift automatically.

Random thought: unify with "session presets" UX we already have — maybe build profiles as an extension of session presets so adoption friction is lower. But session presets today are more client-side; profiles need server routing control.

Quick parking-lot (ideas for later):
- Auto-suggest profile based on first 3 turns of session with confidence threshold.
- Per-org policy library: admins can publish org-approved profiles.
- Marketplace of vetted templates and model-mapping suggestions (like Optimize but for routing).

That’s it for now. Next actions:
- Write a 1-pager for PM review (outline success metrics, scope, risks) — due 2025-11-10
- Slack convo with Mika/Jordan about telemetry schema — tag: #prod-routing
- Create CON ticket for redis perf check (CON-873 exists, reference it)

-- Celeste
